stories.title: Canadians spent $3.3bn less on travel to US in 2025 after Trump’s return to office

The research also indicates that Canadians are not bucking travel overall and instead have replaced US vacations with other international destinations, in a rebuke to Trump’s tariff regime and the president’s continued musings on annexing Canada.

stories.title: Anti-LGBTQ+ laws are on the rise across west Africa, campaigners warn
bullet_points: Activists in the region say politicians regard LGBTQ+ people as ‘the easiest scapegoats to maintain their power’  A growing number of west African countries are implementing or strengthening anti-LGBTQ+ laws, amid local political pressures and a global pushback against LGBTQ+ rights.
In March, Senegal  doubled the maximum prison sentence  for gay sex to 10 years and criminalised the “promotion” of homosexuality.
Niger criminalised  “sexual relations with a person of the same sex”  in February, the first time same-sex intimacy had been outlawed in the country.

stories.title: Tourist plane crashes during flight over Peru’s Nazca Lines, killing 13
bullet_points: Aircraft crashes into field after departing from nearby city of Pisco, according to local authorities  Police in Peru report that 13 people, among them foreign tourists, have been killed in a plane crash in southern Peru, near the Nazca Lines.

Local authorities in Nazca confirmed that 11 tourists and two pilots died when the Cessna Grand Caravan crashed in Pueblo Viejo, approximately 4 miles (6km) from the city of Nazca and roughly 12km from the Nazca Lines site.
